svg.title: Deep learning for antimicrobial peptide prediction - review figure
svg.text: Deep learning for antimicrobial peptide prediction

g.text: hybrids (CNN+BiLSTM+attention) dominate benchmarks — AMPlify · AMP-BERT · this repo
transfer learning from PLMs; GNN variants add predicted structure
Figure 1 | Deep learning for antimicrobial peptide (AMP) prediction. a, Structure–activity basis of AMPs: amphipathic α-helices (Schiffer–Edmundson
projection, hydrophobic moment μH) disrupt bacterial membranes through carpet, barrel-stave and toroidal-pore mechanisms. b, Dual feature tracks: multiple-sequence
alignments and hand-crafted physicochemical descriptors versus contextual protein-language-model (PLM) embeddings. c, Three architecture families with aligned outputs and
their late fusion. d, Benchmarking: ROC/PR analysis and metric comparisons under leakage-free cluster splits. e, Translation pipeline from metagenomes to ranked, validated
leads. f, Open challenges for the field.
